name: Bodily self-determination for competent adults
plainSummary: Competent adults should generally direct decisions about their own bodies, including medical choices, unless a strong overriding reason exists—such as serious harm to others.
whyRoot: The body is the medium through which a person experiences the world; if others controlled it by default, personal agency would mean little. Bodily authority is treated as a root because it pairs moral personhood with a zone of decision-making that others must justify crossing.
description: Foundational claim that competent adults have primary moral and legal authority over their own bodies, including medical choices, absent overriding harm to others.
